item.title: Warriors star Steph Curry claps back at weird podcast criticism of wife Ayesha Curry
item.description: Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry looks on during warmups ahead of a game on Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in San Francisco. (Heather Diehl/Associated Press) HOUSTON - Stephen Curry was evidently none too pleased with social-media chatter around wife Ayesha Curry's first feature-film leading role in the romantic comedy "Second Chance Holiday." A clip from the film, featuring Ayesha Curry giving an on-screen kiss to co-star Matthew Daddario, went viral this past week and served as fodder for a wide variety of podcasts. Former NBA All-Star Gilbert Arenas and former Golden State Warriors backup Nick Young held a 17-minute segment Saturday on the kiss, with Arenas saying "the only blemish in the (Curry) family is the wife." Media personality Emmanuel Acho also devoted a good bit of airtime to the topic. On Wednesday, Curry took to Instagram for a notably pointed response. "I've been hearing a lot of noise, and usually the noise doesn't bother me, doesn't bother Ayesha, but this one in particular - when you're trying to step on the accomplishments of my wife, and obviously needing podcast tapings and topics and giving opinions on somebody else's wife - Nick, (Gilbert), Emmanuel, and anybody else who feels the need to want to have to jump in and give an opinion on something you don't really know about and kinda speaks to a bigger conversation on how you view women in this world and what they're allowed and what they're not allowed to do, even the ignorance behind how acting works," Curry said, cycling through an array of mocking faces. "Obviously, I tried to laugh this one off," he continued. "But something needs to be said. And anytime Ayesha Curry shows up in your headline, I kindly suggest you just give the happy hands, the congratulations, and maybe, just maybe, the apology can be as loud as y'all leading y'all shows with this topic." The video was clearly filmed handheld, at the spur of the moment. A source with direct knowledge of Curry's thinking said that the video response wasn't planned or organized by his team in any way, and came directly from Curry. The majority of Arenas and Young's content centered on the odd idea of Ayesha Curry potentially bringing a negative perception to the Curry family due to her acting career, visibility and independent personal success, a narrative that has existed on social media for years as her husband has simultaneously become one of the most famous athletes on the planet. Curry has increasingly dipped into the Hollywood space in recent years, starring in the animated film "GOAT" and directing the short documentary "The Baddest Speechwriter of All" this year. Back on the court, Curry has led the Warriors to an 8-3 start in 2026-27, averaging 30.6 points, 4.1 rebounds and 4.3 assists in one of the hottest early-season stretches of his career. item.title: Princeton's Kam Mercer officially signs with UC Bearcats basketball
item.description: Almost six months after his commitment was shown on ESPN's SportsCenter , Princeton High School senior Kameron "Kam" Mercer returned to the same room to officially sign with the Cincinnati Bearcats on Nov. 11. It was no surprise, as Mercer has been at UC games and was one of new coach Jerrod Calhoun's priorities when he arrived in town in late March. Mercer helped the Vikings win the Ohio Division I state title on March 22, then Calhoun was introduced as UC's head coach the following day. Mercer had been offered by previous coach Wes Miller's staff in eighth grade. Not long after his introductory press conference, Calhoun was on the phone with Princeton coach Bryan Wyant, asking if his staff had a chance with Mercer. The sales pitch succeeded and Mercer has been "all-in" on UC and Calhoun. After UC's difficult 63-61 loss to Minnesota, Mercer posted on X: "In him I trust" with a picture of himself with Calhoun. During his signing ceremony, he became emotional while talking about his parents, Craig and Nicole Mercer. His mother came to the podium to comfort her 6-foot-5 son. "I believe so much in Calhoun and what he's done," Mercer said. "I know he took a tough loss to Minnesota. I'm not really worried about one game. I'm super excited to get to the next level and play for him. I'm a guy that's going to come in on Day One and be a leader. Somebody that wants to win. I want to become a winner I want to become an NCAA champion." In him I trust🫡. https://t.co/jzYQJqQ4oX — Kameron Mercer (@kameron_mercer) November 10, 2026 Mercer led the Princeton Vikings to a state crown as a sophomore, averaging 14.2 points and 5.4 rebounds per game with 3.4 assists and 2.4 steals per contest. Playing at Huntington Expression Prep in West Virginia as a freshman against older talent, he averaged 11 points, 6 rebounds and 5 assists. He moved up a year scholastically to join the Bearcats for 2027-28. He also attended future teammate Josh Tyson's commitment to UC in September . Tyson played against Mercer at Lakota West but is now playing at La Lumiere in Indiana. Princeton coach Bryan Wyant has been at numerous UC basketball practices and has incorporated some of their strategies into his Vikings. Wyant believes doing so will give Mercer an advantage as a freshman Bearcat. For now, Wyant is very bullish on Mercer. "I think he has a chance to be one of the most dominant players that we've seen in the last 20 years," he said. "I've only been here 20 years, so that's all I can speak for. I'm talking about actual production on the floor. If he can keep progressing, I think he can have a chance at one of the special seasons that we've seen over the last 20 years." item.title: Rams Named Potential Suitor for $108 Million Wide Receiver
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams and head coach Sean McVay entered the 2026 NFL season as Super Bowl favorites to many. What has transpired since has been a nightmare. No, the Rams are not out of playoff contention. In fact, they currently hold a 5-4 record entering Week 10 action against the Arizona Cardinals. What has caused the nightmare if they are still very much alive as a contender in the NFC? Injuries have completely derailed the season that they were supposed to have. Myles Garrett is back, but he has missed most of the season due to a knee issue. Davante Adams is currently out with a ruptured hamstring. Most recently, Puka Nacua went down and is expected to miss extended time due to a knee injury suffered on the final play of last week’s win. At wide receiver, things have gotten bad. It may not help this season, but Los Angeles has been linked as a potential suitor for a $108 million wideout during the offseason. Oct 12, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay reacts during the fourth quarter against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Los Angeles Rams Emerge as Potential Suitor for $108 Million Wide Receiver Bleacher Report has released a new column looking ahead at the top free agents of the upcoming offseason. When it came to Parker Washington, they listed the Rams as one of the top potential landing spots for the Jacksonville Jaguars’ impending free agent. Not only did they named Los Angeles as a team to watch, they also projected that Washington will receive a four-year, $108 million contract in free agency. “While a lack of elite size may keep Washington out of the upper tier of receiver contracts, the 24-year-old should command a deal that falls somewhere between those signed by Wan’Dale Robinson and Alec Pierce this past offseason,” they wrote . Washington would be a huge addition for the Rams. With Davante Adams set to become a free agent as well, he would make perfect sense as a long-term replacement. Back in 2025, Washington had his breakout season with 58 receptions for 847 yards and five touchdowns. In eight games this year, he has racked up 29 receptions for 493 yards and five scores. Washington is just 24 years old right now. He’s going to be one of the most sought after playmakers in free agency. Watch out for Los Angeles as a potential suitor. item.title: UH in the College Football Playoff? Cougars may not have to wait for the expanded 24-team field
item.description: The Houston Cougars and running back Makhi Hughes have a path to the College Football Playoff this season with a No. 14 ranking so far. (Jason Fochtman/Houston Chronicle) The College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams in 2027. If you're the University of Houston , why wait? The Cougars checked in at No. 14 in the latest CFP rankings released Tuesday, a three-spot jump from the previous week. If the playoff began today, the Cougars would miss the cut in the current 12-team format. Under the expanded format for next season - which will include the four champions from the Power Four conferences (SEC, Big 12, Big Ten and ACC), the highest-ranked Group of Six champion and 19 at-large selections - the Cougars would be in position to host a first-round playoff game. How does No. 14 Houston vs. No. 19 Ole Miss at TDECU Stadium sound? Sign up for Cougar Confidential You'll get get in-depth news and analysis about UH's basketball and football teams from reporter Joseph Duarte by signing up for the Cougar Confidential newsletter . "I wanted to have an opportunity to win a national championship," coach Willie Fritz said this offseason about his decision to take the UH job in 2024. That path might be arriving ahead of schedule. To have any chance in this era of college football, you must have an invitation. Otherwise, you can spend your holiday at the Alamo Bowl or Pop-Tarts Bowl. Nothing wrong with those postseason destinations, but the ceiling has been raised for a UH program that is now among the top 15 in the nation. It's been a hard climb. The last time the Cougars were in the national discussion was during the H-Town Takeover, a two-year window that included wins over behemoths Florida State, Oklahoma and Louisville. But even then, the smallest slip (hello, UConn, Navy and SMU) kept the Cougars from a shot at a national title. In the decade since, UH has been mostly irrelevant, going through two different coaches and one bad extension before hiring Fritz, who has been a master program builder at every stop and every level. The Cougars went from 4-8 in his first season to 10-3 last year, capped by a win over LSU in the Texas Bowl. Now, the Cougars enter the final three weeks of the regular season - starting Friday against Colorado in Boulder - still in the hunt for a spot in the Big 12 championship game. UH will need some help - specifically a loss by Texas Tech - and will need to beat Colorado, West Virginia and Baylor. Then leave it up to the computers and tiebreaker scenarios. Under one scenario, UH would win a four-team tie for second place with BYU, Texas Tech and Oklahoma State based on conference opponents' winning percentage. item.title: Frankie Muniz Is ‘Awake and Alert’ After a Daytona Practice Incident — Now He’s Out of Ford’s Veterans Day Exhibition Race With Austin Cindric
item.description: Frankie Muniz, the actor who drives the No. 33 Ford for Team Reaume in the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series, was taken to a local medical facility on Wednesday after an incident during practice at Daytona International Speedway in Daytona Beach, Florida. He was scheduled to partner with Cup Series driver Austin Cindric on the U.S. Air Force team in Ford’s Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic that night. A GT3 race car practicing at Daytona International Speedway in 2023, shown for illustration; it was not involved in Wednesday’s incident. Photo: 350z33 / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) What Team Reaume has said so far Team Reaume announced the transport on X, and NASCAR.com published the statement . It says Muniz “was involved in an incident while practicing for today's Proud to Honor event at Daytona International Speedway” and was “taken to a local medical facility for further evaluation and is awake and alert.” The team added that it would share updates as they become available. Nothing the team, NASCAR.com or the local stations that followed it have published says what happened on track, when it happened, which hospital he was taken to, or whether he was hurt beyond that description. WESH reported that NASCAR Track Communications said Muniz will not take part in Wednesday’s race, which was set for 8 p.m. ET on USA Network. The sources I reviewed do not name a replacement for the Air Force team. The Veterans Day Classic format Ford’s 12-driver lineup sorted the field into six two-driver teams, each running a Mustang Dark Horse R in a livery for one of the six military branches. Muniz and Cindric had the Air Force. Brad Keselowski and Joey Hand were listed for the Army, Ryan Preece and Logan Sargeant for the Navy, Noah Gragson and Layne Riggs for the Space Force, Joey Logano and Ty Majeski for the Coast Guard, and Robert Noaker and Ben Hobson for the Marine Corps. The race itself is short: a 15-minute qualifying session, then 30 minutes on the 12-turn, 3.6-mile road course used for IMSA’s Rolex 24 at Daytona. NASCAR ran points races on that layout in 2020 and 2021, according to NASCAR.com. Ford said the event benefits six nonprofits through the Proud to Honor Fund, and half of ticket proceeds go to Blue Star Families. A 30-minute race leaves little room to rebuild a pairing, and the Air Force team lost one of its two drivers on race day. item.title: Dodgers will be involved in Tarik Skubal's free agency, but will they sign him?
item.description: Scott Boras speaks at a news conference during Major League Baseball's general manager meetings Wednesday in Las Vegas. (John Locher / Associated Press) The Dodgers ’ early offseason to-do list includes a meeting with top free agent Tarik Skubal , the two-time Cy Young winner who they acquired at the trade deadline this year. Other than the Dodgers’ National League Championship Series exit, the three-month fling was as happy of a partnership as either side could have hoped. Skubal jelled with the group immediately, becoming especially close friends with fellow lefty Blake Snell, who promised that he’d worked to recruit Skubal back this offseason. And after posting a 2.61 ERA in 10 starts , Skubal, the Dodgers’ Game 1 starter in both playoff series, limited postseason opponents to a total of three runs. “I know that he enjoyed his time here, we loved having him, so I think that’s certainly helpful as far as these conversations go,” Dodgers general manager Brandon Gomes said Tuesday at General Managers meetings. “And outside of that, he’s earned the right to be in this position and figure out what’s best for him and his family.” That position, while it guarantees him a highly lucrative contract, is complicated by the impending lockout. Skubal’s agent, Scott Boras , when asked during his media availability Wednesday whether he’d consider a shorter deal with a higher average annual value, said he wouldn’t discuss contract negotiations. But creativity around the structure of a deal could help counter teams’ anxieties over a possible salary cap in the next Collective Bargaining Agreement. Read more: Dodgers' Brandon Gomes shares updates on Tarik Skubal, Shoki Oda, Josue De Paula and more It’s clear already that CBA uncertainty won’t fully freeze the market in November. But executives and agents alike have expressed skepticism that the expected lockout will inspire the same kind of spending flurry that arose in 2021, the end of the last CBA cycle. Boras, however, argued against the notion that salary cap talk could put a damper on the superstar market before Dec. 1, when the lockout is expected to go into effect. “Much like 2021, there’s a clear intent on a group of players, and we have no reservations by any teams that they’re going to operate within their abilities and freedoms because they want they don’t want to lose to their competitors,” Boras told reporters. “They want the market to be what it is for them, and they’re utilizing their rights to compete. I think they’re very concerned about losing the opportunity to sign select, key players, and they’re pursuing it aggressively.” The Dodgers are among the teams planning to meet with Skubal, a group that reportedly includes the Mets, Padres and others. item.title: What Reggie Gilliam’s return designation means for the Patriots
item.description: For the first time in five weeks, the New England Patriots had a traditional fullback at practice on Wednesday. Reggie Gilliam, who was initially placed on injured reserve due to knee and ankle injuries in early October, made his comeback during his team’s final session before its trip to Germany for the upcoming Week 10 meeting with the Detroit Lions. This means he is now officially designated to return from IR. Let’s check out how this impacts the Patriots for the time being. Clock starts ticking We will get into the actual on-field impact of a potential Gilliam return to the 53-man roster once/if he is activated. For now, at least, the window for such a follow-up move has been opened. This means that, at least theoretically, Gilliam could be back on the game day roster as soon as this Sunday against the Lions. He will join the rest of the team on the flight to Germany, so there is an option New England could activate him in time for the game. They don’t have to, however: the team has 21 days to make that call before the return window will close again. If not activated at that point, Gilliam would revert back to injured reserve to end his season. Obviously, with return designations limited — more on that in a second — the expectation is is that the 29-year-old will eventually return to the 53-man roster when all is said and done. Two guys, one spot Following Monday’s release of tight end Tanner Arkin — a move that might hint at a potential Gilliam activation given that the rookie served as a stand-in fullback over the last few weeks — the Patriots have 52 of the 53 spots on their active roster occupied. This means that they could easily activate Gilliam without having to make a follow-up move. There is only one problem: he is not the only player currently in the 21-day window. Interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten, who was the next man up after starting right guard Mike Onwenu fractured his ankle in September, returned to practice last week. He too is a candidate to be activated, especially given the current state of New England’s interior offensive line. Fact is, in order to bring both of them back, somebody will have to be removed from the active roster. There are several options, but one of them can effectively be ruled out: a player getting cut. With the Patriots taking their entire healthy roster to Germany, one of the 52 players getting handed his walking papers seems like a highly unlikely outcome. What is more likely is that only one of them will be brought back this week, or that the additional spot for a second activation will be created by moving another player to an injury list. item.description: Tennessee guard Dai Dai Ames (4) shoots between Radford guard Tristan Gross (10) and guard Jordyn Kee (3) during the second half of an NCAA college basketball game, Tuesday, Nov. 10, 2026, in Knoxville, Tenn. | Wade Payne College athletics has spent the past several years trying to figure out how to operate like a professional sports business without actually becoming one. Players are getting paid. Schools are navigating revenue-sharing agreements. Athletic departments are searching for new revenue streams. And lawmakers are attempting to regulate an ever-changing industry. Now, the University of Tennessee men’s basketball team is offering another possible piece of the puzzle. Tennessee players, working with Athletes.org, released a proposed collective bargaining term sheet Tuesday after months of discussions with the school’s athletic department. The exercise wasn’t intended to create a binding agreement. Instead, it was designed to show what a formal relationship between college athletes and their schools could look like. The men’s team elected Tyler Lundblade, Campbell Duncan and DeWayne Brown II to work with the college players’ union on the proposal. Negotiations stretched across August and September before both sides finalized terms on October 1. The proposal could offer a glimpse into where college athletics is headed, particularly as Congress considers new legislation and schools like Utah continue exploring different financial models. It addresses everything from player compensation and health care to transfer rules and offseason commitments. Among its more notable provisions are a salary cap and spending floor, guaranteed compensation for injured players, postseason bonuses, additional medical coverage and mutually agreed-upon transfer portal rules. It would also replace the current patchwork of revenue-sharing payments and university-affiliated NIL deals with a universal athletic services agreement that compensates athletes for playing their sports rather than completing promotional obligations. In other words, it attempts to create something college athletics has largely avoided: a more structured system in which players have a direct voice in determining the rules. Tennessee guard Dai Dai Ames (4) dribbles up court during the first half of an NCAA college basketball game against Radford, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Knoxville, Tenn. | Wade Payne Tennessee athletics chief Danny White has been among the administrators advocating for a CBA as a potential path toward stability in college sports. The proposal isn’t a signed agreement, and Tennessee’s administration hasn’t ratified the terms. But White has publicly supported the exercise, saying that collective bargaining is a proven model in professional sports and could help create a more sustainable future for college athletics. item.title: Browns Predicted to Go Through Another Quarterback Shakeup
item.description: The Cleveland Browns have found it nearly impossible to find a long-term franchise quarterback in recent years. Currently, they have four on the roster and are unsure whether or not any of them are the guy past the 2026 season. Deshaun Watson is the current starter, with Shedeur Sanders as his primary backup. Behind those two options, the Browns have Dillon Gabriel and Taylen Green on the roster. Entering the 2026 season, no one knew what to expect from Watson. He had recovered fully from his Achilles injuries, but his track record in Cleveland wasn’t good. That being said, he has played well so far this season. In eight games played, he has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns, and three interceptions, while also running for 217 yards and a score. Sanders has played in three games, starting last week, and has completed 22 of his 34 attempts for 299 yards, two touchdowns, and no picks. With all of that being said, a new prediction would see the Browns go through yet another quarterback shakeup following the 2026 campaign. Cleveland Browns general manager Andrew Berry watches drills during the first day of rookie minicamp May 8, 2026, at Cross Country Mortgage Campus in Berea, Ohio. Cleveland Browns Predicted to Make Another Quarterback Change Bleacher Report has released a new NFL mock draft following the trade deadline. They are predicting Cleveland to select a new franchise quarterback in the first round. At pick No. 16 overall, they have the Browns selecting Oregon standout quarterback Dante Moore. “Moore is a natural passer with good accuracy and ball placement to operate at a high level from inside the pocket. He is not afraid of big moments and plays with poise. He’s a smooth operator in how he plays with his eyes, feet and mechanics all aligned,” they wrote . “Overall, Moore is an efficient quarterback with smooth mechanics, who could step in and start as a rookie for an NFL franchise.” Moore has played in four college seasons, his freshman year with UCLA and the last three at Oregon. Unfortunately, his 2026 season came to a premature end due a concussion. Overall, he has completed 66.4 percent of his passes for 6,150 yards, 50 touchdowns, and 19 interceptions. No one knows what to expect from Moore at the NFL level. He could become a star down the road or he could be a bust, but the same could be said for any young signal caller. Whether or not the Browns will target a new quarterback in the offseason remains a question mark. Should they choose to do so, Moore could be a serious option. item.title: Treydan Stukes provides silver lining in Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 9 blowout loss to San Francisco 49ers
item.description: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense is searching for answers after giving up 30 or more points for the sixth consecutive game in the Week 9 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . However, the Raiders might have found at least one solution with rookie safety Treydan Stukes. Stukes has been playing well and getting better just about every week, and last Sunday in San Francisco was his best performance to date. The former Arizona Wildcat nabbed his second career interception (first since the season opener) and yielded just 19 yards on five targets (four catches) while coming up with a couple of ‘ defensive stops ’ in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus . That was good enough to earn PFF’s fifth-highest coverage grade (85.8) among safeties for the week. While there’s plenty to be negative about when it comes to the Raiders’ defense, let’s focus on one of the few positives and break down the second-round pick’s outing. Treydan Stukes setting the edge against Trent Williams #Raiders pic.twitter.com/VeXMnHEK2k — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) November 10, 2026 As the numbers above indicate, Stukes’ impact was primarily in coverage against the 49ers. But the clip against the run above caught my eye. San Francisco comes out in 22 personnel with fullback Kyle Juszczyk as one of three strong-side tight ends initially. That’s how Kyle Shanahan likes to run 13 personnel plays/formations while keeping Juszczyk on the field. Meanwhile, the Raiders had the rookie safety cover George Kittle frequently throughout the game, so he’s on the line of scrimmage and on the strong side of the formation. When Juszczyk motions to the weak-side pre-snap, linebacker Quay Walker signals for Stukes to stay inside so that Stukes can cover Kittle with inside leverage if it’s a pass play. The problem with that is it puts a defensive back in the C-gap, where he’s in future Hall of Fame left tackle Trent Williams’ path if the 49ers run outside zone, which is exactly what Shanahan dials up. That’s a mismatch in the offense’s favor since a safety is taking on a block from one of (if not the) best offensive tackles in the game. However, the rookie doesn’t back down. Stukes eyes Kittle initially, and once he reads run, he redirects to take on Williams’ block and ends up resetting the line of scrimmage by winning at the point of attack. That helps force running back Christian McCaffrey to cut upfield and right into linebacker Tommy Eichenberg for a short gain. While Stukes doesn’t make the tackle here, he makes the play by beating a high-quality opponent in a disadvantageous matchup to force the running back to redirect into an unblocked defender. That’s pretty impressive run support from a defensive back. item.title: Cowboys report card: Grading the first half of the season
item.description: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images | Getty Images If the first nine weeks of the regular season were like an amusement park ride for the Dallas Cowboys, they’d be bumper cars. You remember them being great as a kid, so you’re excited to hop in the car and take it for another spin. It’s different. Now that you’re older, the mystique is gone. The gas pedal doesn’t work anymore; sometimes you don’t fit in the car, and you walk out with more back pain than you’ve felt in your lifetime. The defense is the cool bumper car in the corner no one can seem to fix, and the offense is the bumper car that can only turn right. After Brian Schottenheimer’s first year as head coach finished with a 7-9-1 record, it feels as if the team has somehow taken a step back. In the first four weeks of the season, it looked like the offense would carry the defense to the finish line. After three horrible losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Green Bay Packers, and Arizona Cardinals, the Cowboys’ offense struggled to find its identity. There have been some bright spots over nine weeks and a win over the Indianapolis Colts helps, but the report card for the first half of the season isn’t filled with A-grades, despite the roster’s star power. A grades: Quinnen Williams (A): When Quinnen Williams signed his contract extension with the Cowboys this offseason, it set the clock on whether or not the Micah Parsons trade officially pays off. It took Williams some time to find his footing in a system he hasn’t played in since college, but over the last five weeks he looks like an All-Pro at defensive tackle. item.description: (Photo by Rocky Widner/NBAE via Getty Images) Kristaps Porzingis is stepping away from basketball as the Golden State Warriors center continues to deal with health concerns and an ongoing contract dispute with the organization. On Friday, the 31-year-old announced his decision in a statement shared on X, saying his body hasn’t responded as he expected while preparing for the NBA season. "This season I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn't respond the way I anticipated," Porzingis wrote. "I'm doing good, but I know what it takes, and I'm not where I want to be to perform at the level that I expect from myself.
